key_findings.claim: FF Loss as the Primary Indicator in p-type c-Si
key_findings.detail:
In field-degraded p-type modules, FF loss dominates over Isc loss:

| Module | Pmax Loss | Voc Loss | Isc Loss | FF Loss |
|--------|----------|---------|---------|--------|
| Module 1 (mild) | −3.00% | −0.29% | −1.40% | **−1.97%** |
| Module 2 (moderate) | −21.90% | −10.00% | −1.75% | **−19.82%** |
| Module 3 (severe) | −48.67% | −30.31% | −1.75% | **−26.95%** |

- [[papers/Elsevier-498-3124-2-s2.0-85033564380-2018-J-Performance variation of dark current density voltage characteristics for PID affected monocrystalli.pdf#page=3|Wang et al. (2018), p.3]]

FF loss is directly linked to shunt resistance (Rsh) collapse. As Rsh decreases, current bypasses the p-n junction through shunt paths, reducing the FF:
- [[papers/Elsevier-541-3483-2-s2.0-84991699729-2016-J-Microscopic aspects of potential induced degradation phenomena and their recovery processes for p ty.pdf#page=4|Luo et al. (2016), p.4]]

In multicrystalline Si cells under accelerated PID (85°C, 1000 V):

- **Before PID:** FF ≈ 0.75
- **After 1.5 h:** FF ≈ 0.40 (47% reduction)
- **After 2.5 h:** FF ≈ 0.24 (68% reduction)
- [[papers/Elsevier-541-3483-2-s2.0-84991699729-2016-J-Microscopic aspects of potential induced degradation phenomena and their recovery processes for p ty.pdf#page=5|Luo et al. (2016), p.5]]

At higher voltages (−2000 V, 85°C):
- Pmax drops to 20% of initial in 2.5 h
- FF accounts for most of this loss (Isc remains relatively stable)

FF loss is directly tied to shunt resistance collapse:

- **Before PID:** Rsh ~ 1000 Ω
- **After 48 h severe stress:** Rsh ~ 2 Ω (500× reduction)
- **After 491 days recovery:** Rsh = 18.1 Ω (still only 1.8% of original)
- [[papers/Other-81-1747-2-s2.0-85129456088-2022-other-Monitoring the natural recovery of potential induced degradation in poly-crystalline photovoltaic mo.pdf#page=3|Kwembur et al. (2022), p.3]]

The relationship between Rsh and FF:
- $1/R_{sh} = \sigma_0 + \sigma_{sf}(t)$, where $\sigma_{sf}$ is the shunt conductivity from Na-decorated stacking faults
- Full cell performance recovery occurs before $R_{sh}$ fully recovers — meaning FF can recover faster than $R_{sh}$ alone suggests
- [[papers/IEEE-164-2299-2-s2.0-85087499813-2020-J-A Drift and Diffusion Model for PID-s in Solar Modules.pdf#page=4|Schulze et al. (2020), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: Bifacial PERC Front and Rear FF Loss
key_findings.detail:
In bifacial PERC (glass/glass, 136 h, 1000 V, 85°C):

- **Front-side FF loss:** 37–40% (shunting dominant)
- **Rear-side FF loss:** 37–42% (increased surface recombination also degrades FF)
- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=3|Chen et al. (2019), p.3]]

In bifacial HJT modules, rear-side PID is primarily FF-dominated:

- **Rear-side FF loss:** 40.4% Pmax loss after 800 h, primarily from interface recombination at the a-Si:H/c-Si interface
- Front-side PID is Isc-dominated (optical loss from ITO reduction)
- [[papers/Wiley-107-890-2-s2.0-85180462440-2024-J-Potential-induced degradation in bifacial silicon heterojunction solar modules: Insights and mitigat.pdf#page=5|Luo et al. (2024), p.5]]

In perovskite polarization-type PID (800 V, 50°C), FF collapses catastrophically in Stage 2:

- **Stage 1 (0–20 h):** FF 81.09% → 71.89% (11% relative reduction)
- **Stage 2 (20–100 h):** FF 71.89% → 26.86% (63% relative reduction from initial)
- Jsc collapses together with FF; Voc remains stable — characteristic of charge transport disruption at the buried interface, not shunting
- [[papers/Wiley-45-301-2-s2.0-105008480848-2025-J-Failure Analysis of Polarization-Type Potential-Induced Degradation of Perovskite Solar Cells.pdf#page=5|Li et al. (2025), p.5]]

FF recovery tracks Rsh recovery:
- **Recoverable portion (non-ohmic shunts):** FF recovers significantly (up to 95.6% for moderate PID)
- **Non-recoverable portion (ohmic shunts):** Permanent FF reduction of 10–40% in severely degraded cells
- [[papers/Wiley-58-403-2-s2.0-105002608539-2025-J-Identification of Recoverable and Non-Recoverable Potential-Induced Degradation-Shunted Cells in Cry.pdf#page=5|Kumar & Gupta (2025), p.5]]
